newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka strike talks to resume on Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka strike talks to resume on Nov 19.

text.p: Talks between the labour union and management at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, failed to end a six-day strike but will resume on Tuesday, the state radio reported.

The All Ceylon Commercial and Industrial Workers Union, and the Employers Federation of Ceylon will resume negotiations on Tuesday to resolve the strike, the Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation reported.
Union and management officials were not immediately available for comment on Monday's talks.
The labour stoppage came after Shell Gas Lanka suspended nine employees following a breach of safety regulations at Colombo port when gas was being unloaded.
The strike caused gas shortages for city and suburban consumers, the daily Observer newspaper reported.

Shell Overseas Investment BV, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, bought a majority stake in the state-owned gas monopoly in October 1995 for $37 million under the government's programme to privatise state enterprises.
The company is currently embroiled in a controversy with the government after it increased the price of domestic gas twice in one year, in apparent violation of the privatisation deal.

The Public Enterprises Reforms Commission, which handles privatisations, has said Shell was given a five-year gas distribution monopoly under the privatisation deal on condition that prices could only be raised by 10 percent a year.
